proof_scope: Live extraction regression guards for resolved pdf_oxide issues. Each corpus case drives the real extractor over the real source PDF named in its issue and asserts that the specific defect stays fixed. Commands run with this fixtures/ directory as the working directory. Deterministic unit-level cases guard recently fixed ordering and table-assignment assumptions that protect the live extraction paths. Dependency-audit cases run the real cargo-audit scanner against the real lockfile.

claims.proves: the named defect in each referenced issue does not reproduce on the current build, and the library suite stays green; each case was observed failing on the pre-fix code before being accepted
claims.does_not_prove: full-document extraction accuracy, semantic correctness beyond the asserted predicate, or that unrelated PUA-emitting fonts such as Wingdings are handled. Wingdings is an explicit unsupported policy until a fixture-backed Wingdings encoding table exists; this crate currently has Symbol and ZapfDingbats encoding tables but no Wingdings table. Dependency-audit guards prove scanner output for the current lockfile only; they do not prove replacement of the intentionally open ttf-parser dependency.

cases.name: issue-21-symbol-pua-bullet-decodes
cases.description: NASA SP-2016-6105 p19 ships SymbolMT as Type0/Identity-H whose ToUnicode CMap maps the bullet straight to U+F0B7. That Private Use Area codepoint must not survive into extracted text, and the anchor paragraph must still be extracted -- a zero PUA count with no anchor block would only prove the paragraph was dropped. Observed pre-fix: exit 1, U+F0B7 present, block_type Body. Observed post-fix: exit 0, bullet decoded, block_type List. Issue: https://github.com/grahama1970/pdf_oxide/issues/21 Extended: the same run also asserts requirement (2) — the bold run-in heading is marked as run_in_lead ('Technical Management Processes:') on the anchor block.

cases.name: issue-21-checker-still-detects-pua-negative-control
cases.description: Adversarial control against a blind checker. Page 38 of the same PDF carries 16 U+F0D8 codepoints from ADKAIK+Wingdings-Regular, which this crate deliberately does NOT map (no Wingdings encoding table). The checker must therefore exit 1 there and name the codepoint. If this case ever starts exiting 0, the detector has gone blind and the positive case above proves nothing. This is not hypothetical: an earlier version of the check used a regex character class whose escape degraded to a literal hyphen, so it counted U+002D and would have reported a clean page either way.

cases.name: issue-3-nested-list-item-segmentation
cases.description: NIST 800-53r5 p46 (0-based 45): AC-2 items e.-h. and the numbered children of h. must materialize as separate item-level list blocks, not merged runs. Root cause was merge_list_runs_and_continuations absorbing ANY same-x List sibling; the guard now restricts sibling absorption to symbol-bullet runs (which must keep merging, per closed issue #28) while explicit enumerated markers a./1./(a) stay separate. Verify is the in-tree corpus test, which was observed failing before the guard and passing after. Issue: https://github.com/grahama1970/pdf_oxide/issues/3

cases.name: issue-6-flowchart-text-survives
cases.description: 800-53Ar5 p46 flowchart: the five texts issue #6 recorded as lost must all survive extraction. Matching normalizes the document's own encoding -- NFKC for fi/ffi ligatures and U+019F 'Ɵ' for the 'ti' pair ('NoƟfy', 'AcƟon'), which PyMuPDF reproduces identically, so it is the PDF's ToUnicode, not extractor damage. The original loss report and an earlier re-test both missed the Ɵ quirk and counted surviving text as lost. Issue: https://github.com/grahama1970/pdf_oxide/issues/6

cases.name: issue-2-page45-annotation-requirements
cases.description: NIST 800-53r5 AC-1 page (0-based 44): item-level list materialization each-exactly-once with no Related Controls absorption, labeled_enhancements + nist_control_enhancements_none, section_link + nist_quick_link, exactly one unsplit AC-1 heading, and no chrome-text leakage. Item 1's original one-merged-region criterion is superseded by issue #3's item-level contract (1fd6c066); a merged view belongs to downstream structural grouping, not core. Issue: https://github.com/grahama1970/pdf_oxide/issues/2

cases.name: issue-20-bbox-space-stamped-and-convention-proven
cases.description: Issue #20: every bbox-bearing artifact declares its coordinate space. A live annotation call (1512.03385v1) and a live snapshot page (NIST 800-53r5 p45) must both carry a bbox_space stamp valid against contracts/bbox_space_v1.schema.json, and the declared convention pdf_points_bottom_left_xywh is proven against a PyMuPDF search-rect oracle: the bottom-left reading must contain the anchor line and the top-left reading must not (the honesty half keeps the checker falsifiable). Measured before stamping existed: block top edge 593.4 vs oracle 595.8 bottom-left; top-left off by ~500pt. Issue: https://github.com/grahama1970/pdf_oxide/issues/20

cases.name: p19-char-dedup-glyph-loss
cases.description: Char-dedup glyph loss: deduplicate_overlapping_chars dropped any glyph within 2pt of the previous glyph's x-origin regardless of identity; spaces are ~2pt wide so the first glyph after a narrow space was deleted ('privacy'->'rivacy', 'mapped'->'apped', 'establishes'->'stablishes', 'federal'->'ederal' on NIST 800-53r5 printed p19). Dedup now requires the SAME character. Guard asserts glyph-count parity between extract_chars and extract_spans and intact words in the lattice serialization. Observed failing pre-fix (35 vs 36 'p' glyphs, four truncated forms) and passing post-fix.

cases.name: census-word-fidelity-sweep
cases.description: Every alphanumeric token PyMuPDF extracts on each of the 55 census pages must have the same Counter multiplicity in pdf_oxide extract_text (NFKC + document 'Ɵ' normalization). This upgrades the old 4+-letter word-set guard and records the current positioned-region Counter gap separately so it cannot be mistaken for per-region proof.

cases.name: census-text-loss-apply-requires-token-counter-preflight
cases.description: Applying a text-loss resolution must run the live token Counter sweep before the ledger can be updated. This uses an invalid empty-evidence decision so the command exercises the preflight but writes no ledger change.

cases.name: issue-21-symbol-pua-unit-guards
cases.description: In-tree guards for FontInfo::normalize_symbol_pua. Cover the Symbol bullet mapping (Symbol 0xB7 is bullet U+2022, not middle dot U+00B7, so subtracting 0xF000 is wrong) and the deliberate non-mappings: non-symbol fonts, Wingdings, already-real Unicode, out-of-window codepoints, and multi-character expansions. Also runs detect_run_in_lead guards (bold-colon lead accepted; all-bold lines, colon-less leads, and late-bold emphasis rejected).
command: cd .. && cargo test --lib normalize_symbol_pua 2>&1 | grep 'test result:' && cargo test --lib detect_run_in_lead 2>&1 | grep 'test result:'

cases.name: mcid-sequence-and-table-gap-assignment-guards
cases.description: Issue #39 guard for two reviewer-identified assumptions: the NIST census page set must not contain duplicate TextSpan.sequence values inside the same MCID group, sort_mcid_spans_reading_order must not alias line assignments when synthetic duplicate sequence values are present, and character-level table assignment may retain glyphs centered in narrow ruling gaps but must not force glyphs from wide gutters into the nearest cell.
command: cd .. && PYTHONPATH=python:scripts/pdf_lab .venv/bin/python scripts/pdf_lab/check_mcid_sequence_uniqueness_issue39.py && cargo test --lib duplicate_sequence_values_do_not_alias_line_assignments 2>&1 | grep 'test result: ok. 1 passed' && cargo test --lib gap_glyph 2>&1 | grep 'test result: ok. 2 passed'

cases.name: extract_text_branch_parity_debug_vs_release
cases.description: Issue #33 guard for the tagged NIST SP 800-53r5 PDF: debug and release builds must take the same top-level PdfDocument::extract_text branch on every page. The checker runs the real extract_text example in both profiles with PDF_OXIDE_BRANCH_TRACE enabled, parses the JSONL branch decisions, and diffs every predicate except the expected profile label. Observed pre-fix: debug returned a partial structure tree and used structure_order_cached on page 0, while release fell back to content_stream_order.

cases.name: issue-38-ligature-vs-decomposed-double-draw
cases.description: Ligature double-draw hole in identity-based char dedup: one draw layer emits the 'fi' ligature (U+FB01) and the duplicate layer emits decomposed 'f' + 'i' across the same advance, so identity comparison keeps every glyph and the visible text doubles. Observed pre-fix on the reverted logic: ligature-first yielded 'fix' as "\ufb01fix" and decomposed-first yielded "fi\ufb01x"; post-fix both collapse to a single rendering. Guard also pins the two non-goals: a real letter starting at or past the ligature's advance is kept, and the narrow-space glyph guard from the p19 fix still holds.
command: cd .. && cargo test --lib -- ligature_then_decomposed_double_draw_is_deduplicated decomposed_then_ligature_double_draw_is_deduplicated ligature_dedup_keeps_legitimate_adjacent_letters ligature_dedup_does_not_reopen_narrow_space_glyph_loss 2>&1 | grep 'test result: ok. 4 passed'

cases.name: issue-36-nist-appendix-grid-small-caps-cells
cases.description: Issue #36 guard for NIST SP 800-53r5 appendix-grid cells on printed pages 457, 464, and 486. The live checker extracts the real PDF through the shared table path and asserts that five rows no longer contain duplicate control IDs, truncated small-caps prefixes, or footer/watermark contamination. It also writes a p457 AC-4(17) char/span dump so the first failure mode remains inspectable.

cases.name: issue-35-nist-withdrawn-row-note-cells
cases.description: Issue #35 guard for NIST SP 800-53r5 appendix tables on printed pages 474 and 481. The live checker extracts the real PDF through the shared table path and asserts that withdrawn-row notes spanning the implemented-by and assurance columns are serialized as one readable note cell with no orphaned continuation text in the assurance cell.

cases.name: issue-37-cross-document-reading-order
cases.description: Issue #37 cross-document guard for the reading-order repair surface. The integration test builds four non-NIST minimal PDFs with Type0/Identity-H text and explicit ToUnicode CMaps, then runs the real PdfDocument::extract_text path and compares extracted order against tests/fixtures/issue37_cross_document_expected.json for RTL Hebrew, bidirectional Latin/Hebrew, math-like super/subscript runs, and rotated text.

cases.name: issue-34-census-adjudication-events-derived-status
cases.description: Issue #34 guard for the NIST historical census ledger. The checker replays append-only adjudication events, proves projected current_status counts remain stable, and runs the deterministic reconciler over an adjudicated entry with missing evidence to prove it writes deterministic_status without overwriting the event-derived current_status.

cases.name: issue-15-paste-absent-from-cargo-audit
cases.description: Issue #15 guard for RUSTSEC-2024-0436. Run the real cargo-audit scanner against the current Cargo.lock and assert that paste is not reported while the intentionally open ttf-parser advisory remains visible for issue #17. This catches regressions where optional dependencies or default image features reintroduce paste.
command: cd .. && cargo audit --json > /tmp/pdf_oxide_issue15_agentic_eval_audit.json && jq -e '(.vulnerabilities.found == false) and ([.warnings.unmaintained[]?.package.name] == ["ttf-parser"]) and (([.warnings.unmaintained[]?.package.name] | index("paste")) == null)' /tmp/pdf_oxide_issue15_agentic_eval_audit.json

cases.name: full-lib-suite-no-regression
cases.description: Font decoding sits on the hot path for every extraction, so any change there must leave the whole library suite green. Baseline when this case was written: 4623 passed, 0 failed.
